_note: Sourced from NASA Human Research Program (HRP), NASA ISS Medical Operations Flight Rules, and Space Flight Human-System Standard (NASA-STD-3001). A value inside 'green' is normal, inside 'yellow' but outside 'green' is watch, outside 'yellow' is act. 'hazard' is one of the four spaceflight hazards (radiation, isolation, gravity, environment); 'nasa_risk' names the NASA HRP risk it maps to. 'source' is continuous vs manual.

indicators.name: Heart rate
indicators.reference: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Cardiovascular Adaptations & Host-Microorganism Interactions; ISS nominal resting range 60–100 bpm.
indicators.how_to_measure: Measured continuously via the crew biometric wristband (optical photoplethysmography) and verified during cycle ergometer (CEVIS) exercise using ECG chest electrodes.
indicators.why_it_matters: In microgravity, cephalad fluid shift unloads the cardiovascular system. Heart rate changes indicate autonomic deconditioning, orthostatic stress, dehydration, or systemic infection.

actions.yellow: Log 30-minute rest, consume 500 mL electrolyte fluid pouch, repeat resting heart rate check, and review recent exercise telemetry.
actions.red: Cease physical exercise countermeasures immediately, assume resting recumbent posture, provide supplemental O2 if symptomatic, and initiate immediate consultation with Flight Surgeon.

indicators.name: Heart rate variability
indicators.reference: NASA HRP Behavioral Health & Performance (BHP) Standard Measures: rMSSD autonomic index (nominal range: 30–150 ms).
indicators.how_to_measure: Calculated continuously from root mean square of successive differences (rMSSD) of R-R intervals captured by continuous biometric band during rest and deep sleep cycles.
indicators.why_it_matters: HRV is the primary biomarker for autonomic nervous system tone. Suppressed HRV reflects persistent sympathetic dominance, cumulative operational stress, fatigue, or early subclinical infection.

actions.yellow: Review workload schedule with mission planning, implement 15-minute guided relaxation countermeasure, and monitor subsequent sleep cycle HRV recovery.
actions.red: Flag severe physiological or psychological strain to Medical Officer; mandate schedule offload, circadian lighting adjustment, and private psychological conference.

indicators.name: Blood oxygen
indicators.reference: NASA Flight Medicine Crew Baseline & ISS Environmental Life Support System (ECLSS) Standard (nominal: 95–100%).
indicators.how_to_measure: Monitored continuously through transmissive pulse oximetry on the wearable biometric wristband, with spot checks via fingertip oximeter if signal quality falls.
indicators.why_it_matters: Detects arterial hypoxemia caused by ECLSS cabin oxygen scrubber anomalies, elevated cabin CO2 partial pressure, or pulmonary microvascular congestion during spaceflight.

actions.yellow: Cross-check cabin ambient O2/CO2 telemetry, verify sensor positioning, take 5 slow deep diaphragmatic breaths, and repeat measurement.
actions.red: Don portable breathing apparatus (PBA), confirm cabin atmospheric pressure and O2 concentration, and notify commander for immediate ECLSS cabin review.

indicators.name: Temperature
indicators.reference: NASA HRP Immunology Evidence Report: Spaceflight-induced immune dysregulation. Dermal thermal limits (nominal: 35.5–37.5 °C).
indicators.how_to_measure: Monitored continuously via infra-red / thermistor dermal sensor array on the wearable biometric band, calibrated for circadian fluctuations.
indicators.why_it_matters: Spaceflight induces significant immune dysregulation, increasing susceptibility to latent virus reactivation (EBV, VZV) and bacterial transmission in closed volumes. Elevated temperature indicates systemic infectious stress.

actions.yellow: Hydrate with electrolyte fluid, perform Photo Check on any noticeable rash or lesion, take oral temperature confirmation, and monitor febrile trend.
actions.red: Quarantine bedding, initiate on-board blood/swab diagnostic cartridge, and report to Medical Officer for antimicrobial and antipyretic protocol.

indicators.name: Sleep
indicators.reference: NASA HRP Human Health Countermeasures: Sleep Loss & Circadian Desynchronization Evidence Base. Recommended mission sleep: 7.0–9.0 hours.
indicators.how_to_measure: Derived automatically from actigraphy sleep-wake algorithms on the wearable band, tracking sleep onset, awakenings, and total sleep duration.
indicators.why_it_matters: Microgravity, pump noise, and absent 24-hour solar cycles disrupt slow-wave sleep. Chronic sleep deprivation rapidly degrades cognitive speed, situational awareness, and manual docking precision.

actions.yellow: Adjust cabin dynamic lighting schedule to blue-depleted evening spectrum 2 hours before sleep; avoid digital display glare; verify sleep compartment acoustic barriers.
actions.red: Mandate 60-minute daytime nap schedule offload, consult Flight Surgeon for consideration of non-habit-forming sleep aid countermeasure.

indicators.name: Blood pressure (systolic)
indicators.reference: NASA Cardiovascular Laboratory ISS Clinical Reference Guidelines (nominal systolic: 90–120 mmHg).
indicators.how_to_measure: Measured daily during morning checkout using the automated pneumatic brachial cuff, with astronaut positioned in seated neutral body posture.
indicators.why_it_matters: Cephalad fluid redistribution temporarily increases carotid arterial pressure before compensatory diuresis decreases circulating blood volume by 10–15%, altering systemic vascular resistance.

actions.yellow: Repeat cuff measurement after 5 minutes quiet seated rest; log sodium and water intake for the preceding 12 hours.
actions.red: Report reading to Medical Officer; check for postural dizziness; review lower body negative pressure (LBNP) exercise schedule.

indicators.name: Blood pressure (diastolic)
indicators.reference: NASA Cardiovascular Laboratory ISS Clinical Reference Guidelines (nominal diastolic: 60–80 mmHg).
indicators.how_to_measure: Measured concurrently with systolic pressure using automated brachial blood pressure cuff during daily health routine.
indicators.why_it_matters: Diastolic pressure reflects peripheral vascular resistance and coronary perfusion pressure during cardiac relaxation, which changes as vascular compliance adapts to microgravity.

actions.yellow: Re-check cuff placement, confirm resting state, verify fluid hydration balance.
actions.red: Alert Medical Officer; record concurrent heart rate and ECG strip to assess cardiac fill time.

indicators.name: Blood glucose
indicators.reference: NASA Nutritional Biochemistry Laboratory: Standard Spaceflight Metabolic Indices (nominal fasting: 70–100 mg/dL).
indicators.how_to_measure: Measured via capillary fingerstick glucose test strip or minimally invasive continuous glucose sensor cartridge during scheduled metabolic check-ins.
indicators.why_it_matters: Metabolic adaptation, spaceflight insulin resistance, and inadequate caloric intake alter glycemic regulation, affecting physical endurance and cognitive performance during EVAs.

actions.yellow: Review dietary intake log; consume balanced nutrient pouch with complex carbohydrates and protein; re-test in 2 hours.
actions.red: Check for symptoms of hypoglycemia (tremor, diaphoresis) or hyperglycemia; administer oral glucose countermeasure if low; contact Flight Surgeon.

indicators.name: Mood
indicators.reference: NASA Behavioral Health and Performance (BHP) Standard Self-Assessment Scale (1=Severely Stressed, 5=Optimal/Thriving).
indicators.how_to_measure: Logged once daily during morning digital check-in on crew tablet interface via validated 5-point Likert psychological status scale.
indicators.why_it_matters: Early detection of confinement-related stress, interpersonal tension, sensory deprivation, and mission fatigue prevents acute behavioral incidents in isolated vehicle environments.

actions.yellow: Encourage private Earth uplink call (family/friends), utilize onboard VR nature immersion countermeasure, schedule recreational downtime.
actions.red: Notify Commander and Medical Officer; initiate dedicated private psychological conference (PPC) with terrestrial ground support.

indicators.name: Radiation dose
indicators.reference: NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) & NCRP Report 186: Career Dose Limits for Spaceflight. Nominal background: 0.0–1.0 mSv/day.
indicators.how_to_measure: Continuously tracked via crew Personal Radiation Dosimeter (CPD) and internal vehicle area silicon pixel detectors (Timepix/IV-TEPC).
indicators.why_it_matters: Outside low Earth orbit, Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) and Solar Particle Events (SPE) carry high ionizing potential, causing DNA double-strand breaks and escalating lifetime fatal cancer risk.

actions.yellow: Verify active dosimeter status, inspect solar activity telemetry from Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) / SWPC feed.
actions.red: Sound Solar Particle Event alert: crew immediately moves to high-density storm shelter area (water wall / logistics module); seal storm hatches.

indicators.name: Cabin CO2
indicators.reference: NASA ISS Environmental Life Support System (ECLSS) Flight Rule: Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide Limits (nominal: 0.0–3.0 mmHg).
indicators.how_to_measure: Continuously monitored by cabin non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) atmospheric analyzers placed throughout active module ventilation loops.
indicators.why_it_matters: In microgravity, absence of thermal convection allows exhaled CO2 to form stationary pockets around sleeping astronauts. High CO2 causes space headaches, lethargy, and cognitive impairment.

actions.yellow: Check cabin ventilation diffusers, increase module inter-cabin ventilation fans, inspect Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly (CDRA) scrub cycle.
actions.red: Switch auxiliary amine CO2 scrubbers to maximum; relocate crew to higher-ventilation module; don emergency portable oxygen masks if symptoms persist.
